summary: A tachometer and boost pressure on the factory windshield HUD (experimental)
author: inotbarnacle (packaged by NBTApps)
description:
Draws a curved tachometer and the boost pressure on the car's factory windshield head-up display (HUD), with an on/off switch under My Vehicle. The author calls it experimental.

What it does
- A curved tachometer from 0 to 8,000 RPM, thicker from 6,700 RPM, and boost as a number in PSI, beside what the HUD already shows
- Check Show HUD gauges under My Vehicle → HUD Gauges to turn it on. It stays on after you leave the menu until iDrive next restarts, and starts off again after that. Uncheck it to clear the HUD
- It reads engine speed and boost from the engine control unit and sends nothing to it. It writes only to the HUD's display
- It steps aside while the car's own navigation uses the HUD, and clears the HUD while LaunchDeck is open
- While BoostDeck or ShiftDeck is open, it shows what that app reads instead of reading it itself. ShiftDeck reads the engine speed only, so there is no boost then

What you need
- An NBT Evo head unit with iDrive 6 (ID6), on a software version the app was built for (see Good to know)
- NBTApps agent 1.6.0 or later
- A factory windshield HUD that the app works with. It is made for the author's reference car, a 340i (F3x) on NBTevo_N18032I
- The car's diagnostic gateway. The app tries 169.254.21.3, and if nothing answers there, looks for the gateway on the car's wired network

After installing
The iDrive screen restarts. Open My Vehicle, choose HUD Gauges, and check Show HUD gauges. Try it first with the car parked.

Good to know
- Owners of an F06 and an F16 report that their HUD refuses the overlay. The menu then says the HUD rejected it. Other HUDs have not been tried
- If the HUD shows something wrong, uncheck Show HUD gauges. If the menu does not open, remove the package and restart iDrive
- The gauges stay on while you drive. Turn them off if they distract you
- It does not start on a head unit with native Android Auto (NBT-AAD) installed, even while Android Auto is not running, or with CarPlay Advanced and its HUD hook
- Earlier versions remembered whether it was on. This one does not, and removing the package also removes the file they saved
- This package does not check the head unit's software version. The author's own installer checks the head unit's iDrive framework files, and accepts those of these NBTevo versions only: K17052I, L17252I, M17345I, M17365I, N18032I, N18092I, O18184I, P18362I, Q18491I, R19101I, R19144I, S19221I, S19322I, T18501I, T21424I, T23235J, T24081I, U19384I, V20153I, W20204I, X20511I, Y21432J, Y22292I, Y23236I and Y24073J. On another version the menu may not load
- If the app was put on this car before, with the author's desktop installer or by hand, uninstall it the same way first. NBTApps refuses to install over it
- If the app does not find the car's diagnostic gateway, put its address in a gateway-ip.txt file on the head unit: /var/opt/hmi/data/ID5/gateway-ip.txt for all of the author's apps at once, or one in the app's own folder. The shared file comes first. This package writes neither
- This is a pre-release: the package has not yet been installed on a car through NBTApps

HUD Gauges is by inotbarnacle, free of charge. Its menu is under the MIT License. The program that draws on the HUD uses NBT-AAD's HUD and MOST code by nanaisu, under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0, so it may not be sold. Both licences are in the package. NBTApps packages the author's own builds, unchanged, with the author's agreement. It comes as it is: you install it at your own risk.
